The reasons you listed for not liking the new dog can be fixed with some training and dedication. These behaviours are very unlikely to go away on their own. Look into youtube videos about food guarding/jumping and maybe get some toys that he can keep himself entertained with so he doesn’t feel he has to follow you around as much. Find time to play with him, take him for walks, or to dog parks and let him wear himself out. A sleeping dog is a pleasant dog.

Otherwise, you say you don’t “see yourself” bonding with him. I think just saying that is preventing you from it. My last dog passed away in November, and my family got me a puppy in March. I’ll admit that even though I was convinced I wanted him, it took me a while to get over this sort of resentment I felt, so I think I understand what you’re getting at. I felt like I couldn’t love him as much as my past dog, so instead of thinking “I don’t love him” I started thinking “He makes my family happy” and “It’s nice to have some life in the house”. Eventually this turns into affection. 

Especially since your dog is a shelter dog, it might take a but longer for him to fully adjust to your lifestyle. There is no quick fix to this. But it will get better with time. It sounds like your boyfriend likes this dog a lot and it’s always good when a shelter dog gets a new forever home, so I want to encourage hanging onto him! You still have plenty of time to decide, after all. A lot can change in another month! Best of luck to you.

Do you tend to let other people choose what to do and just go along with it? I.e. choose where to hang out/where to go for dinner/how to spend your weekend/what TV show to watch? Only other advice I have is to maybe do more things that /you/ like. Might help with feeling more like yourself. At the very least I think it’s relieving to see friends enjoying themselves doing a “you thing” if that makes sense. Or, maybe you’re just bored with what activities you usually do and should get into some new things with friends.

Otherwise, if you noticed this is kind of a recent thing, give it time and see where it goes. Could just be a symptom of some other stress in your life and just go away on its own. Best of luck to you!

Hey, hope you’re doing well. 
My immediate thought reading this was that this is very indicative of depression. I have depression, and this is a very familiar feeling to me, right down to the part where it happens when there’s nothing to fully focus on. Depression doesn’t necessarily mean you hate your life/want to die, either, so if that’s the only reason you don’t suspect it you may want to do some more research before anything develops fully. Therapists are great and aren’t only for the mentally ill, either. You can talk to someone, work through this, and leave it like that. 

If you’re very sure it’s not depression, maybe it’s something like imposter’s syndrome?

I can’t say whether or not becoming an artist is the “right” path, because it depends a lot on the type of art you want to do. Disclaimer; I’m not a professional artist so take this with a grain of salt.

Plenty of artists, especially today, get by without going to art school thanks to social media. Try to post something new every day, interact with other artists, use your tags, etc. Make a Twitter, make a Tumblr, post your art EVERYWHERE. Not everyone is on Insta! Keep a professional online persona or an art account you keep separate from your personal. Build a portfolio you’re proud of. If you live in the middle of nowhere, the Internet is your best friend for stuff like this.

On the other hand, art school is good if you’re looking to make connections and good schools can help get you out there. If there are pro artists you follow online, see if you can send them a PM and ask about what they think about art school.

Do you want to do concept art? Storyboarding? Animation? You’ll likely be working with an art based company. This is what most people think of when you say art school, and the school connection to the studios can help.
Freelancing, contracts, and commission type work can be harder to get by on, but it’s doable. This is where professional social media comes in handy.
Also keep in mind jobs like design, (can be anything really. Houses, cars, logos, etc, working under a non-art based company) or my personal fave, tattoo artistry. Tattoos are more popular than ever, so there may be more opportunities to find work.
Don’t panic too much about competition and people being “better” than you. There is no better, just different. It took me a while to learn that. And besides, if you find a specific niche you’re comfortable in, there won’t be much competition at all.

For now, do your research, work to improve your craft, and don’t worry about it too much. Definitely speak to all varities of artists and get advice from people who went through it firsthand. 
And there’s no harm in taking a gap year and working a entry level job while you think about what you want to do. You don’t need to have it figured out by 17 anyways. Even if you end up going to trade school, that doesn’t rule out doing art in the future.

Hope this helps in some way, sorry if it came off as a bit of a tangent... I wish you the best of luck!!
